arxiv-2012-14681.title: Faster Re-translation Using Non-Autoregressive Model For Simultaneous Neural Machine Translation
arxiv-2012-14681.creator: Hyojung Han, Sathish Indurthi, Mohd Abbas Zaidi, Nikhil Kumar LakumarapuBeomseok Lee, Sangha Kim, Chanwoo Kim, Inchul Hwang
arxiv-2012-14681.description: Abstract Recently, simultaneous translation has gathered a lot of attention since it enables compelling applications such as subtitle translation for a live event or real-time video-call translation. Some of these translation applications allow editing of partial translation giving rise to re-translation approaches.

arxiv-2203-06646.title: Understanding mass hierarchy in collisional energy loss through heavy flavor data
arxiv-2203-06646.creator: Bojana Ilic 1 and Magdalena Djordjevic 1
arxiv-2203-06646.description: Abstract While experimental observations, such as the mass hierarchy effect, are attributed and analyzed within radiative models, their interpretation crucially depends on collisional energy loss contribution, which is often neglected in such analyses. To our knowledge, neither a (direct) simple relation between collisional energy loss and heavy quark mass is established, nor an observable that quantifies this effect.

arxiv-2208-12323.title: Large Volatility Matrix Analysis Using Global and National Factor Models
arxiv-2208-12323.creator: Sung Hoon Choi, Donggyu Kim
arxiv-2208-12323.description: Abstract Several large volatility matrix inference procedures have been developed, based on the latent factor model. They often assumed that there are a few of common factors, which can account for volatility dynamics. However, several studies have demonstrated the presence of local factors.

arxiv-2210-02516.title: Equalizing Credit Opportunity in Algorithms: Aligning Algorithmic Fairness Research with U.S. Fair Lending Regulation Conference: Proceedings of the 2022 AAAI/ACM Conference on AI, Ethics, and Society; August 1–3, 2022; Oxford, United Kingdom Proceedings of the 2022 AAAI/ACM Conference on AI, Ethics
arxiv-2210-02516.creator: I. Elizabeth Kumar, Keegan E. Hines, John P. Dickerson
arxiv-2210-02516.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by I. Elizabeth Kumar, Keegan E. Hines, John P. Dickerson. Credit is an essential component of financial wellbeing in America, and unequal access to it is a large factor in the economic disparities between demographic groups that exist today.

arxiv-2404-04591.title: C 0 C^{0} Lagrangian monodromy
arxiv-2404-04591.creator: Noah Porcelli
arxiv-2404-04591.description: Abstract We prove that (under appropriate orientation assumptions), the action of a Hamiltonian homeomorphism ϕ \phi on the cohomology of a relatively exact Lagrangian fixed by ϕ \phi is the identity. This extends results of Hu-Lalonde-Leclercq [ 7 ] and the author [ 10 ] in the setting of Hamiltonian diffeomorphisms.

arxiv-2406-14956.title: Unlocking the Global Synergies in Low-Rank Adapters
arxiv-2406-14956.creator: Zixi Zhang, Cheng Zhang, Xitong Gao, Robert D. Mullins, George A. Constantinides, Yiren Zhao
arxiv-2406-14956.description: Abstract Low-rank Adaption (LoRA) has been the de-facto parameter-efficient fine-tuning technique for large language models. We present HeteroLoRA , a light-weight search algorithm that leverages zero-cost proxies to allocate the limited LoRA trainable parameters across the model for better fine-tuned performance.

arxiv-2408-04289.title: EMTeC: A Corpus of Eye Movements on Machine-Generated Texts
arxiv-2408-04289.creator: Lena S. Bolliger, Patrick Haller, Isabelle C. R. Cretton, David R. Reich, Tannon Kew, Lena A. Jäger
arxiv-2408-04289.description: Abstract The E ye Movements on M achine-Generated Te xts C orpus (EMTeC) is a naturalistic eye-movements-while-reading corpus of 107 native English speakers reading machine-generated texts. The texts are generated by three large language models using five different decoding strategies, and they fall into six different text type categories.

arxiv-2411-00470.title: Higher homological algebra for one-point extensions of bipartite hereditary algebras and spectral graph theory
arxiv-2411-00470.creator: Karin M. Jacobsen, Mads Hustad Sandøy, Laertis Vaso
arxiv-2411-00470.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Karin M. Jacobsen, Mads Hustad Sandøy, Laertis Vaso. In this article we study higher homological properties of n n -levelled algebras and connect them to properties of the underlying graphs. Notably, to each 2 2 -representation-finite quadratic monomial algebra Λ \Lambda we associate a bipartite graph B Λ ¯ \overline{B_{\Lambda}} and we classify all such algebras Λ \Lambda for which B Λ ¯ \overline{B_{\Lambda}} is regular or edge-transitive.

arxiv-2412-08972.title: RuleArena : A Benchmark for Rule-Guided Reasoning with LLMs in Real-World Scenarios
arxiv-2412-08972.creator: Ruiwen Zhou, Wenyue Hua, Liangming Pan, Sitao Cheng, Xiaobao Wu, En Yu, William Yang Wang
arxiv-2412-08972.description: Abstract This paper introduces RuleArena , a novel and challenging benchmark designed to evaluate the ability of large language models (LLMs) to follow complex, real-world rules in reasoning. Covering three practical domains—airline baggage fees, NBA transactions, and tax regulations— RuleArena assesses LLMs’ proficiency in handling intricate natural language instructions that demand long-context understanding, logical reasoning, and accurate mathematical computation.

arxiv-2501-01457.title: Reinforcing Thinking through Reasoning-Enhanced Reward Models
arxiv-2501-01457.creator: Diji Yang, Linda Zeng, Kezhen Chen, Yi Zhang
arxiv-2501-01457.description: Abstract Large Language Models (LLMs) exhibit great potential in complex multi-step reasoning through inference-time thinking but still struggle with deciding when to stop thinking due to limited self-awareness about their knowledge boundaries. While human preference alignment has shown extraordinary opportunities, expensive labeling challenges adherence to scaling law.

arxiv-2505-04447.title: Warming up the Fibres
arxiv-2505-04447.creator: Dibya Chakraborty, and Rudnei O. Ramos
arxiv-2505-04447.description: Abstract Fibre inflationary models are constructed in type-IIB string flux compactification. These models have been shown to be in agreement with the cosmological observations under appropriate choices of parameters, which originate from their string theory construction. In the present work, we embed such models, originally studied in the cold inflation picture, in the context of warm inflation.

arxiv-2509-18239.title: Are X-Ray Detected Active Galactic Nuclei in Dwarf Galaxies Gamma-Ray Bright?
arxiv-2509-18239.creator: Milena Crnogorčević, Tim Linden, Annika H. G. Peter
arxiv-2509-18239.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Milena Crnogorčević, Tim Linden, Annika H. G. Peter. The γ \gamma -ray emission from active galactic nuclei (AGN), including both beamed blazars and misaligned-AGN, dominates the extragalactic γ \gamma -ray point-source population count and flux. While multi-wavelength studies have detected an increasing number of AGN within dwarf galaxies in the local Universe, γ \gamma -ray emission has so far only been associated with systems hosting supermassive black holes (SMBHs).

arxiv-2512-06188.title: Potential theory and applications in conformal geometry
arxiv-2512-06188.creator: Shiguang Ma
arxiv-2512-06188.description: Abstract . In this paper, we want to give an exposition of our recent work on linear and nonlinear potential theory and their applications in conformal geometry. We use potential theory to study linear and quasilinear equations arising from conformal geometry. We establish the asymptotic behavior near singularities and derive applications in conformal geometry.

pmc-11688721.creator: Xuexin Yu, Laura Zahodne, Alden Gross, Belinda Needham, Kenneth Langa, Lindsay Kobayashi

pmc-12379413.title: Bullying and depression serially mediate the association between perceived gender nonconformity and suicidality among US adolescents: a theory driven intersectional analysis
pmc-12379413.creator: Michael G. Curtis, Melanie Mason, Joshua Boe, Ysabel Beatrice Floresca, Shahin Davoudpour, Noah A. Jayne, Lauren Beach, Gregory Phillips
pmc-12379413.description: BackgroundAdolescent suicidality has become an alarming public health concern. Perceived gender nonconformity has been identified as a risk factor for suicidality. Several factors (e. g. bullying and depression) have been posited as potential mechanisms through which perceived gender nonconformity is associated with suicidality; however, nascent research indicates instability in these associates due to youth’s exposure to intersectional forms of marginalization.

pmc-12538742.title: Network meta-analysis of high tibial osteotomy combined with different bone defect filler materials for medial compartment knee osteoarthritis
pmc-12538742.creator: Zhiwei Pei, Aixian Tian, Baoxin Zhang, Zijian Lian, Xinlong Ma
pmc-12538742.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). ObjectiveThis study aims to systematically review and analyze the clinical and radiographic outcomes of high tibial osteotomy (HTO) combined with various bone defect filler materials for the treatment of medial compartment knee osteoarthritis (MCKOA).

pmc-12628979.title: Effects of in utero tobacco exposure, age of smoking initiation, and environmental pollution on the risk of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease in adulthood: a large scale prospective cohort study
pmc-12628979.creator: Jianing Li, Guoxian Li, Ze Ma, Ziqing Sun, Yujie Shi, Zexin Lou, Hanqing Zhao, Mengtong Sun, Yu Wang, Qida He, Miao Jiang, Yueping Shen
pmc-12628979.description: BackgroundThere has been limited research to date comprehensively assessing the effects of in utero tobacco exposure, age of smoking initiation and environmental pollution on the incidence of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD).MethodsThe participants in the current study were drawn from the UK Biobank cohort.

pmc-13265164.title: A bibliometric analysis of global research in cervical cancer radiotherapy (2015–2024): trends, hotspots, and future directions
pmc-13265164.creator: Yue Hou, Yu Gao, Wen-Ming Yan
pmc-13265164.description: BackgroundDespite the growing volume of cervical cancer (CC) research, few bibliometric studies have specifically focused on the recent landscape of radiotherapy—a critical treatment modality. This study aims to examine the global research landscape, thematic focus areas, and emerging trends in CC radiotherapy from 2015 to 2024 through a bibliometric and visual analysis.

pmc-13397625.title: The impact of job satisfaction among healthcare workers in township hospitals in Western China: a case study of Lanzhou City
pmc-13397625.creator: Sheng Li, Guoai Yao, Fei Wang, Qing Jia, Minmin Jiang, Jinyu Wang
pmc-13397625.description: ObjectiveTo investigate the factors influencing the job satisfaction of healthcare workers in primary healthcare institutions in Lanzhou City.MethodsA stratified random cluster sampling method was used to conduct an online survey among healthcare workers in township health centers across five districts and three counties of Lanzhou City.
